entries.original: A normal transvaginal ultrasound does not exclude endometriosis.
entries.summary: A normal internal pelvic ultrasound cannot rule out endometriosis.
keyPoints: A normal internal pelvic ultrasound cannot rule out endometriosis.

entries.original: Endometriosis cannot be ruled out by a normal transvaginal ultrasound.

entries.original: A normal MRI does not establish that endometriosis is absent.
entries.summary: A normal MRI cannot rule out endometriosis.

entries.original: Serum CA-125 should not be used to diagnose endometriosis.

entries.original: Cycle-related pelvic pain and pain during sex keep endometriosis among the considerations, but do not confirm a diagnosis.
entries.summary: Pelvic pain related to periods or pain during sex can fit endometriosis, but does not confirm it.
keyPoints: Pelvic pain related to periods or pain during sex can fit endometriosis, but does not confirm it.

entries.original: Pain or bleeding in early pregnancy may warrant early-pregnancy assessment, but these symptoms alone do not identify the cause or confirm ectopic pregnancy. The urgency of referral depends on the overall clinical presentation.
entries.summary: Pain or bleeding in early pregnancy may need assessment, but symptoms alone cannot identify the cause or confirm ectopic pregnancy.
entries.nextConsideration: The overall clinical picture determines how urgently assessment may be needed.

entries.original: A single serum hCG result does not exclude ectopic pregnancy after an indeterminate transvaginal ultrasound; the available evidence does not support generating an individualized serial-testing schedule.
entries.summary: One blood pregnancy-hormone result cannot rule out ectopic pregnancy after an inconclusive internal pelvic ultrasound. This evidence cannot provide an individual repeat-testing schedule.
keyPoints: One blood pregnancy-hormone result cannot rule out ectopic pregnancy after an inconclusive internal pelvic ultrasound.
